item.title: VIREX: The Immersion & Integrity Overhaul
item.description: A massive update focusing on information density, deep system tweaks, and a complete UX refinement.
item.content:encoded:
We've spent the last few days stripping away the filler and focusing on what matters. Improved information density, professional utility, and deep immersion.

Readme: Information Density

  • Bio Overhaul: Replaced the filler cards with a Biography and Mission section.
  • PGP Integration: Added my official PGP Fingerprint directly to the header.

Lens: The Full Rewrite

  • Navigation Overhaul: Destroyed the overlapping floating buttons.
  • Typography Sync: Swapped the "dev mono" headers for the expressive site-wide display typography.
  • Optimized Lightbox: Removed the aggressive blurs and fixed description cutoffs.
  • Bento Layout: The photography archive now uses a dynamic Bento layout.

Tweaks & Immersion

  • Dynamic Identity: Added a Dynamic Favicon that listens to your theme accent.
  • Focus Mode (Zen): Full-immersion mode with top/bottom depth-of-field blurs.
  • Brutalist Mode: For when you're tired of squircles. Every corner now has a 0px radius.
  • Developer Font: Global override to JetBrains Mono.

Performance & Utility

  • Lens Optimization: Reduced total image assets from ~200MB to ~40MB using WebP.
  • Loom Deep Search: Upgraded documentation viewer to pre-fetch markdown files.
  • PWA Support: The site is now fully installable on mobile and desktop.
  • RSS Feed Compatibility: You can now add the Virex blog as an RSS feed!
  • Deep SEO: Implemented dynamic OpenGraph tags and JSON-LD structured data.

"True perfection is attained not when there is nothing more to add, but when there is nothing more to take away."

Love you all <3

item.title: Basic Cybersec And How To Not Be A Victim
item.description: The internet is a hostile environment. Protecting yourself doesn't require a degree, just discipline.
item.content:encoded:
1. Password management is a must-have.

    Use a password manager to generate and store complex passwords.

  2. You need to enable MFA!

    Avoid SMS-based codes. Use an authenticator app or a physical security key.

  3. Software updates are your best defense!

    Developers release updates to patch security vulnerabilities.

  4. Avoid phishing attacks.

    Be skeptical of EVERY link. Go directly to official websites.

  5. Public Wi-Fi is dangerous.

    Don't use it for sensitive tasks without a trusted VPN.

Security Table

ToolPriorityStatus
A Password ManagerCritical✓
MFAHigh✓

"security is a process, not a product."

item.title: Long Term Pixel 10 Pro Use: My Review of the Tensor G5 Architecture
item.description: A deep dive into the 3nm transition and why the Pixel 10 Pro is finally a consistent daily driver.
item.content:encoded:
Architectural Maturity: The TSMC Shift

Moving to TSMC's 3nm process makes efficiency gains immediately apparent. Thermals are stable.

Memory and Multitasking

16GB of LPDDR5X RAM handles aggressive background processes without killing cached apps.

Camera & Computer Vision

The new ISP allows for 100x Pro Res zoom using on-device generative models. Video Boost is now handled locally on the TPU.

Platform Stability

Android 16 builds are surprisingly performant. The level of control in the modern Android stack is peaking.

item.title: The web is cooked (..And we are the ones smelling the smoke)
item.description: Why does a site need more processing power than the apollo 11 moon landing??
item.content:encoded:
The modern web is basically malware.

I saw a landing page with 12MB of JavaScript. For three buttons and a logo.

  • 60% of load time is just analytics scripts.
  • We have frameworks to fix performance issues caused by other frameworks.

I built virex.lol to be fast. If your site takes more than 2 seconds on 4G, you didn't build a website.

item.title: Your cloud is just someone elses computer.
item.description: This is why i hoard data (and you should too).
item.content:encoded:
Stop trusting corporations with your data.

  • If it's on my drive, no one can "un-license" it.
  • Paying $15/month for a library that changes every week is a joke.
  • I keep games, movies, and tools because once they're gone from the web, they're gone FOREVER.

It's about digital sovereignty. They don't care about your files, they care about your subscription.

item.title: Why I actually use Arch.. (and it's not for the meme)
item.description: I just want a system that doesnt hand bs over to me...
item.content:encoded:
• No bloat: exactly what I need and nothing else.
  • The Wiki: the holy grail of documentation.
  • Rolling release: latest kernel features immediately.

My rig (RX 6800 XT / i5-14600K) runs much better when I own the hardware instead of the OS owning me.

item.title: The internet is dead.
item.description: If you think you are talking to real people on the big platforms anymore, I have a bridge to sell you.
item.content:encoded:
This is why I self host.

Socials are just bots talking to bots.

  • AI-generated slop consumed by AI-generated scrapers.
  • "Blue checks" with generic AI names replying to everything.
  • Algorithms showing what keeps you scrolling, not what is good.

AI already killed the world wide web. Go outside.
